chunks: And whatever was in it from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Ashʿarī—may Allah be pleased with him—I have narrated it from my father, and from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan—may Allah be pleased with them both—from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah and ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī together, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Ashʿarī.

key_terms.أَبِي: my father; one of the author’s immediate transmitting authorities
key_terms.الْأَشْعَرِيِّ: al-Ashʿarī; a nisbah identifying Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā in the chain
key_terms.الْحِمْيَرِيِّ: al-Ḥimyarī; a nisbah identifying one narrator within the chain
key_terms.جَمِيعًا: together; indicates joint transmission from both named narrators
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; indicates the author’s act of narration through a sanad/isnad

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain of Shaykh al-Ṣadūq to Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Ashʿarī in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits narrations from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Ashʿarī. It serves as a technical chain-of-transmission notice in hadith literature, documenting the intermediaries between the compiler and this narrator.
